inferior pubic ramus: Lower ramus of the pubis; it joins the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus.
inferior rectus muscle: Turns the eye down (depression) and in, and rotates it outwards; oculomotor nerve. It can be trapped in orbital floor fractures.
inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps fe: Inferior subtendinous bursa of biceps femoris
Between the biceps femoris tendon and the fibular collateral ligament.
inferior tarsus: Connective tissue plate forming the skeleton of the lower eyelid; narrower than the upper one.
inferior thyroid notch: Shallow notch in the middle of the lower border of the thyroid cartilage.
inferior thyroid tubercle: Prominence at the lower end of the oblique line; the infrahyoid muscles attach to it.
inferior transverse scapular ligament: Ligament bridging the spinoglenoid notch; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it into the infraspinous fossa.
inferior vertebral notch: Notch below the pedicle; forms the upper half of the intervertebral foramen.
infraglenoid tubercle: Prominence below the glenoid; the long head of triceps arises here.
infrapatellar fat pad: Fat pad behind the patellar ligament, between the capsule and the synovium; it fills the joint space during knee movements.
infraspinatus muscle: Rotator cuff muscle from the infraspinous fossa to the greater tubercle; rotates the arm laterally. Suprascapular nerve.
infraspinous fossa: Fossa below the spine; infraspinatus arises here.
infratemporal surface of greater wing: Surface of the greater wing facing the infratemporal fossa; the upper head of lateral pterygoid arises here.
inguinal ligament: The folded lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis, running from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle; the femoral neurovascular bundle and iliopsoas pass beneath it.
inner lip of iliac crest: Inner lip of the iliac crest; transversus abdominis and quadratus lumborum attach to it.
innermost intercostal muscles: Deep layer of the internal intercostals; the intercostal neurovascular bundle runs between this muscle and the internal intercostal.
interclavicular ligament: Joins the medial ends of the two clavicles across the jugular notch.
intercondylar area: Area between the two condyles on the tibial plateau.
intercondylar eminence: Prominence between the condyles; the cruciate ligaments attach around it.
intercondylar fossa: Deep notch between the two condyles; the anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments attach here.
intercondylar line: Line separating the intercondylar fossa from the popliteal surface; the joint capsule attaches to it.
intercornual ligament: Small ligament joining the sacral and coccygeal cornua.
intercuneiform interosseous ligaments: Strong ligaments between the facing surfaces of the cuneiforms.
intermediate cuneiform bone: The smallest cuneiform; the base of the 2nd metatarsal locks into it, giving the Lisfranc joint its stability.
intermediate sacral crest: Ridge formed by the fused articular processes.
intermediate tendon of digastric muscle: Tendon joining the two bellies; a fibrous loop binds it to the body of the hyoid.
intermediate zone: Line between the inner and outer lips of the iliac crest; internal oblique attaches to it.
intermuscular gluteal bursae: Bursae between gluteus maximus and vastus lateralis.
internal abdominal oblique muscle: Middle-layer muscle beneath the external oblique, with fibres running up and forwards; in males its lower fibres give rise to cremaster. Nerves: T7–L1. It flexes the trunk and rotates it to the same side.
internal intercostal membrane: Membranous continuation of the internal intercostal muscle posteriorly towards the spine.
internal intercostal muscles: Muscles whose fibres run at right angles to the external intercostals; they depress the ribs in forced expiration.
internal occipital crest: Midline ridge on the inner surface of the occipital bone; the falx cerebelli attaches to it.
internal surface of squamous part of fro: Surface of the frontal bone facing the brain; it carries the frontal lobe.
interosseous border of radius: Sharp border facing the ulna; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.
interosseous border of tibia: Border facing the fibula; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.
interosseous border of ulna: Sharp border facing the radius; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.
interosseous crest of fibula: Border of the fibula facing the tibia; the interosseous membrane attaches to it.
interosseous membrane of forearm: Fibrous membrane joining the radius and ulna; its fibres run down and medially from the radius, transferring load from the hand to the ulna.
interosseous membrane of leg: Fibrous membrane joining the tibia and fibula; it separates the anterior and posterior muscle compartments of the leg and gives attachment to muscles.
interosseous metacarpal ligaments: Interosseous ligaments between the metacarpal bases.
interosseous sacro-iliac ligament: One of the strongest ligaments in the body, between the tuberosities of the sacrum and ilium; it locks the sacroiliac joint.
interpubic disc: Fibrocartilaginous disc of the pubic symphysis; it usually contains a small cavity.
intersesamoid ligament: Joins the two sesamoid bones under the big toe.
interspinales colli muscles: Short muscles between adjacent cervical spinous processes.
interspinales lumborum muscles: Short muscles between the lumbar spinous processes.
interspinales thoracis muscles: Interspinous muscles of the thoracic region; often present only at the upper and lower ends.
interspinous ligaments: Thin ligaments between adjacent spinous processes; they limit flexion.
intertransverse ligaments: Thin ligaments joining adjacent transverse processes; they limit lateral flexion.
intertrochanteric crest: Ridge joining the trochanters behind; the quadrate tubercle lies on it.
intertrochanteric line: Line joining the trochanters in front; the hip joint capsule and iliofemoral ligament attach to it.
intertubercular sulcus: Groove between the two tubercles; the tendon of the long head of biceps runs in it.
